description: Curated psychotropic and alcohol-use-disorder medication reference for clinician mode. Original wording; FDA label facts summarized, never copied. Names, RxCUIs, brand lists and boxed-warning flags were checked against live RxNorm, openFDA and MedlinePlus Connect on lastVerified.
scope: Clinician mode only. Education to support medication-referral conversations; not prescribing, dosing, switching or tapering guidance. Medication decisions belong to a prescriber (psychiatrist, primary care clinician or psychiatric nurse practitioner).

usedFor.label: Bipolar I disorder: acute manic or mixed episodes and maintenance

Interacts with lamotrigine (raises its levels) and other anticonvulsants.

usedFor.label: Bipolar I disorder: maintenance to delay mood episodes

clinicianNotes: Not a dopamine blocker; nausea, vomiting, constipation, indigestion and tachycardia are common.

CNS depressant effects (sleepiness, confusion) add to alcohol, opioids and other sedatives; the label also includes a suicidality warning and fetal-harm caution.
Short, fixed treatment course taken orally.

medications.class: Neuroactive steroid (GABA-A receptor positive modulator), intravenous
clinicianNotes: Boxed warning: excessive sedation and sudden loss of consciousness; given only as a continuous intravenous infusion in a certified healthcare setting with pulse-oximetry monitoring (REMS).
The manufacturer announced it would stop US distribution (2024); confirm current availability. Oral zuranolone is the other approved option for postpartum depression.

clinicianNotes: People must be opioid-free before starting; it precipitates opioid withdrawal and blocks opioid pain relief (relevant for planned surgery or pain care).

Liver injury is uncommon but monitored; the injection can cause injection-site reactions.
